evals.prompt: My pre-push gate failed with working-tree-iteration-only right after I rebased onto main. The diff only changes api/handler.go, but the gate output points at files I never touched. Triage it.
evals.expected_output: Untracked or generated artifacts are moved to a hold directory outside the repository under a restore trap, the identical gate command is rerun, and it passes; the artifacts are restored and no code commit is created.
expectations: The exact gate command and working-tree-iteration-only mode are recorded before any change.
Untracked artifacts are moved, not deleted or overwritten, to a hold directory outside the repository.
A restore trap is installed before the move and the artifacts are restored afterward.
The same gate command is rerun unchanged and its exit code is reported.
No code or feature commit is created for a pure workspace-contamination failure.

evals.prompt: The merge gate still fails in clean-checkout mode after I quarantined the build artifacts, on an assertion in pkg/parse/reader_test.go. My branch only touched api/handler.go. Can I just rerun until it passes or should I ignore it?
evals.expected_output: Git blame on the exact failing lines shows the defect predates the merge base and that the current diff does not touch those lines; the defect is fixed in a separate commit on top of the feature branch and the unchanged gate reruns green.
expectations: The failing assertion and its file and line range are identified before editing.
git blame is run on the exact failing lines and the blamed commit is checked against the merge base.
The current diff is shown not to touch the failing lines or fix site.
The fix is a separate commit, not an amendment or squash into the feature commit.
The same gate command is rerun and exits zero after the fix.

evals.prompt: Gate fails clean-checkout on the new assertion in reader_test.go. The branch rewrote the parser function that assertion covers, and blame on those lines points at my latest feature commit. I think it is the rebase. Confirm and fix.
evals.expected_output: The failure is classified as feature-caused because blame places the failing lines inside the current diff; the fix is made in the feature commit and no separate inherited-defect commit is created.
expectations: Blame evidence is used to check whether the failing lines belong to the current diff.
The skill does not label the failure as inherited or change-independent when blame points at a current-diff commit.
The fix is applied in the normal feature change rather than a separate inherited-defect commit.
The same gate command is rerun to confirm the result.

evals.prompt: One of my new unit tests fails with a stack trace pointing at the exact function I just wrote. Help me debug the null dereference.
evals.expected_output: The merge gate triage workflow is not selected; the failure is already localized by the stack trace to the current change.
expectations: The skill is not selected for an ordinary localized test failure.
No quarantine, gate rerun, or git blame triage is proposed.
